title: The transit link is down at both ends
scenario: R1 Gi0/1 at 10.0.99.1/30 connects directly to R2 Gi0/1 at .2/30. Users behind R1 cannot reach R2’s server LAN. Both routers are available through independent console access. These are representative current records.

exhibits.title: R2 current configuration/state
exhibits.text:
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 10.0.99.2 255.255.255.252
 shutdown
State: administratively down/down

exhibits.title: R2 relevant event
exhibits.text: %LINK-5-CHANGED: Gi0/1 changed state to administratively down

question: Which correction addresses the demonstrated configuration fault?
options: Apply no shutdown to R1 without checking the already enabled local interface.
Replace the transit cable before addressing the displayed far-end shutdown.
Restore the intended no-shutdown state on R2 Gi0/1.
Change both transit masks to /24 while leaving R2 shut.
explanation: R2's current shutdown configuration and administrative state identify the disabling of the transit. Enabling only R1 or changing masks cannot override R2's shutdown; the evidence does not yet justify replacing the cable. Restore the approved far-end state, then verify both ends, routes and the original client service.
fix:
```ios
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
R2(config-if)# no shutdown
R2(config-if)# end
R2# show ip interface brief
```

Check R1’s state and routes separately, test from the affected PC, and save after verification.

title: The transit-source test works while client traffic fails
scenario: PC-A is 10.0.10.50/24, gateway R1 10.0.10.1. R1/R2 transit is 10.0.99.1/.2 on /30. SRV is 10.0.20.10/24 with gateway R2 .20.1. R1 has the intended route to the server; no policy routing is configured.

exhibits.title: R1 paired tests
exhibits.text:
Source 10.0.99.1 to SRV succeeds
Source 10.0.10.1 to SRV fails

exhibits.title: R2 complete installed forwarding prefixes
exhibits.text:
10.0.99.0/30 connected Gi0/1
10.0.20.0/24 connected Gi0/0
Local /32 interface routes only; no other route or default

question: Which demonstrated missing dependency explains the source difference?
options: R1 has no route toward the server network.
R2 has no route to the client-source subnet.
SRV has no local gateway configured.
explanation: R2 can return toward the transit-source .99.1 over a connected route, but no listed prefix matches .10.1 or .10.50. Unlike the source-test result alone, the complete route evidence establishes this missing return route.
fix:
```ios
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# ip route 10.0.10.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.99.1
R2(config)# end
R2# show ip route 10.0.10.50
```

On R1 separately:
```ios
R1# ping 10.0.20.10 source 10.0.10.1
```
Then verify PC-A by address, name, and actual service before saving.

title: Transfers slow on a 100-Mb/s link
scenario: SW1 Fa0/24 connects to R1 Gi0/0. The approved lab design pins both endpoints to 100 Mb/s full duplex. Transfer performance declined after a change. Counters below cover the same current observation interval.

exhibits.title: SW1
exhibits.text:
Fa0/24: 100 Mb/s, half duplex
Late collisions: 100→135

exhibits.title: Neighbor evidence
exhibits.text: CDP reports local not-full duplex and peer full duplex

question: Which correction follows the stated design and evidence?
options: Set SW1 Fa0/24 to the intended matching 100/full settings.
Change R1 to 1000/full while retaining SW1 at 100/half.
Clear counters without changing either operational duplex.
Restart both devices before saving the mismatch evidence.
explanation: The displayed settings directly establish a duplex mismatch. Correct the one deviating endpoint in this explicitly fixed-speed design, then compare fresh increments under a controlled transfer. This does not establish that every other aspect of the link is fault-free.
fix:
```ios
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/24
SW1(config-if)# speed 100
SW1(config-if)# duplex full
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/24
```
Preserve previous counters, verify both endpoints, repeat a bounded transfer, and compare new errors before saving.
